I genuinely loved the OG Xbox but did not feel the same about the 360. It focused on everything I did not want or didn’t care for. The “pros” listed in the article (Partychat, dashboard, over-emphasis on digital downloads) are all what I’d consider irrelevant at best, negatives at their worst. The roster of unique games and game-types populating the original machine saw a steep decline as eveything seemed to homogenize into a vision dictated by corporate suits, a vision of what they think gamers should want, not necessarily what we actually wanted.

People seem to forget it was during the latter half of the 360 generation which marked the beginning of the decline of Xbox, not the Xbone’s launch. This was the gen the suits took control (probably because they saw how profitable the business could be when you’re actually on top winning and moving units). Once CorpoSoft was at the wheel, it was all downhill from there.

Exclusives, ambition and superior versions.

Pixel shaders. A lot of people don’t even know what they are, but they are the reason the visual quality jump from the previous generation to that one was so huge and why we have not seen anything like it since. We have seen a slow gradual fidelity increase, but it’s likely we won’t ever again see such a generational leap in a single day.

Streamlined online okay was also huge. Even to this day, with the amazing advancements in Steam APIs, nothing comes close in PCs to the streamlined nature of the console ecosystem matchmaking that was introduced that generation. PC gamers still to this day rely on multiple apps.

The introduction of achievements was also huge. Ignoring the OCD obsession to 100% a title, having these “digital footprints” made gaming experiences feel a lot more… social, even in single player games.

It also was the first console to open itself to indie developers, even if still drastically restricted for today’s standards. The impact this had on mainstream gaming should never be understated.

The technology and the games it made possible. Both PC and consoles were pushing the rendering tech forward. People were anxious to get their hands on the next jump in gaming tech (and phone and TV).

I grew up with the Xbox 360: getting it at or close to launch, watching the intro to Tony Hawk Project 8 over and over. Weekends at my cousin's house where we spent entire days and nights playing COD MW2, Black Ops, MW3, and BO2. Playing GTA 4 and blowing myself up with rockets, laughing hysterically as Niko flew through the air. Red Dead, sneakily playing Godfather 2 because of the club where you could see the topless ladies. Forza, Project Gotham; this was the era where I played online the most too with friends from school; during Summers I would play from the moment I woke up to the time my Dad got home from work; he knew I played all day because the 360 was warm. Good times.

The online system was so well thought out. It wasn't the first console to offer online play, but it was the first to do it really well. I ended up playing games online with the same friends I used to game with as kids/teenagers, when we'd all go round to one person's house, except now we were playing online from our own houses. It was just leagues ahead of what Sony and Nintendo were doing.

I remember buying a PS3 and there was no private chat, party chat, or cross-game chat, some games had no mute options cos it wasn't a system-wide feature, there were no live updates to show what your friends were playing, and there were no cross-game invites either. So while the PS3 had some great single player games, I never used it for online games that weren't exclusive cos it made no sense to.

Obviously the 360 had great games, and typically the best versions of cross-platform games (excluding PC of course), all with achievements and no forced installs. The online store got 2-3 new XBLA games every week, all with demos that unlocked via unlock keys, so if you liked the game you could buy it and not have to re-download it.

The first couple of hardware revisions were noisy/rattly and failure-prone, but everything else was so good that people put up with it. It's a shame the launch model wasn't like the 360 S or 360 E, cos then it would be hard to criticise it at all.

The Xbox 360 is simply one of the best and most influential consoles of all time. As time has gone by, its legacy and influence has grown exponentially. It was the first to have a storefront on console. It lead the way in championing indie games and making the transition to digital consumption. Achievements spawned trophies on PlayStation. Party chat, another key feature first on Xbox 360, would arrive on PlayStation an entire generation later (Nintendo only recently adopted it lol). Then you have the games; so many of them great and diverse. Single player, multiplayer and co-op were all covered on 360. People talk about PS4 being the true successor to PS2 (to skip over the disappointment of PS3) but in all honesty it was the true successor to the Xbox 360. It did what the 360 did but better and more improved. I recall Microsoft bundling early 360 models with a free headset. Sony did likewise on PS4 (remember the one ear piece?). Even competitors took notes from it. That is the legacy of the Xbox 360.

There’s more I can say about the 360 particularly regarding where Microsoft got it wrong and how that lead to their current situation but that’s for another time.

@Balaam_ That's exactly how I see it. That generation was the beginning of the corporatization of the industry. Shareholders saw games like San Andreas and Halo 2 decimate Hollywood box Office revenue and decided they're was a profit to be milked from it (which sadly they're just recently starting to realize those limitations and have decided to neuter our industry instead of going the hell away themselves.)

We started to see fewer original IP, visuals homogenized into the piss filter that the generation became famously known for, and there were fewer and fewer risks with every game. Worse, we began seeing the sterilization of gameplay mechanics as more and more studios began seeking mainstream appeal with handholding features like quest markers, fast travel, and losing the ability to tailor your experience like killing important NPCs or dropping quest-related items even if you had no idea what purpose they served.

What's worse is hardware nerds got in on it and we saw gaming go from being about fun games to maxing out frames and resolution. There has always been a drive for graphical fidelity, but never to the extent that we've seen the past 3 generations and especially not on the console front where we've always accepted trading quality for affordability.

The Xbox 360 featured an exclusive title called Lost Odyssey, arguably the greatest JRPG ever created. While most JRPGs are aimed at a younger audience and tend to feature straightforward, simple narratives, Lost Odyssey takes a different approach. Its core, titled "A Thousand Years of Dreams, A Thousand Years of Memories"—which explores the protagonist’s past—was penned by Kiyoshi Shigematsu, a recipient of the prestigious Naoki Prize. These stories delve into universal themes: the experience of loss and separation, a profound sense of emptiness, and the sorrow of having neither a place to return to nor a destination to head toward. Much of this content is written with those in the twilight of their lives in mind.The main storyline is also rooted in the personal tragedies experienced by the project’s executive producer, Hironobu Sakaguchi.The game boasts a top-tier creative team, including character designs by Takehiko Inoue (Slam Dunk, Vagabond) and a musical score by Nobuo Uematsu—some of the finest talent to ever work on an Xbox title.Even today, many fans continue to hope for a remake or a sequel.

#4148. Best Upgrades To In Probably Stolen

Running a business means learning how to delegate your budget for things that improve your store, whether that's more space for inventory, higher quality contacts and connections in your network, or improved security and attractiveness in your storefront. These real-world responsibilities carry over into the cyberpunk world of Probably Stolen...with some additional things to consider that you're probably not thinking about in the real world (at least, I hope not).

After meeting Joe Wild on day seven, you gain access to his network, which functions as the upgrades menu for the game. Here, you can gain access to new business opportunities, expand and improve your storefront, and get some help with the more...delicate aspects of running a store in a seedy part of the station. There are a lot of options to choose from, so here's a basic rundown of where to start.

There are a total of 51 upgrades available for your shop in Probably Stolen, though you can't get all of them at the same time; some upgrades lock out other options (for example, you can't have the Power Line Hijack and Makeshift Reactor perks at the same time).

Wild's suite of upgrades can be roughly categorized into seven sections:

Run the best storefront in the Lower Levels with these Probably Stolen beginner tricks.

On your first run of Probably Legal, you can pretty much get whatever upgrades you like as you explore how the game works and what each option does. that being said, a few things will make your life a little easier, especially as your learn mechanics.

Firstly, please get the Dossier upgrade. I know it doesn't sound particularly exciting or important, but trust me, you run out of room so quickly in that thing when you're hanging onto all of the tutorial documentation for reference. It's a great place to store your appraisal tools and identification documents, as well, so having more room there is a definite plus.

After that, I'd go with a relatively quick and easy money-making option; the easiest of these are the Red Imp Brewery, water trading, and hydroponic farming. The Red Imp Brewery will send you a case of beer every week that sells for roughly 18 credits a pop, which is quick, convenient, and legal, so it won't cause you any trouble with any faction. With water trading, you can always have a supply of water to sell or use in farming, which can be especially good if you hit an event that causes water to become more valuable (such as the water treatment plant going down). Hydroponic farming requires only the base machine, seeds, water, and power, and can make you a lot of product quickly if you can get your levels just right; it's less complicated than other trades, so a great way to start learning how they work.

Finally, I'd opt for the Power Line Hijack perk (your power service is free and you don't have to worry about generator maintenance) and then go through the upgrade tree for Dr. Jackson's shop to give yourself access to better equipment and machines.

If you're doing a fully-legal run of Probably Stolen, you won't need to use Joe's people at all; you can ignore their upgrades completely. You can also ignore the chemist contact and chemistry trade entirely, as they produce illegal goods.

I'd recommend really leaning into a trade for your money here. Pick up whichever trade you like the most; hydroponics, water trading, wine making, aquaculture, and rat wrangling are all legal, so they're all on the table. As I said, water and food are your most reliable early game moneymakers, so whether you stick with them or not, you might want to invest in them earlier on to build up your finances.

You'll also want to invest heavily in your store's attractiveness and security. Get all three Store Renovation and Showcase Expansion upgrades to max out your shop's base attractiveness and your ability to bring in customers, then stack on a mirage projector for even greater effect. You could then get the vending machine and vending fountain for added streams of income. You'll also want to invest in insurance and the security alarm system to protect your store from thieves, and pay your janitorial fees to keep that attractiveness level high.

Now for something completely different. If you're doing an illegal run of Probably Stolen, you need to be invested in contraband; weaponry and drugs will make you the most money, but they're also some of the most dangerous items in the game. This is the kind of run where you're going to need Joe's people the most often. Invest early in the Inspection Early Warning Service and try to keep enough credit on hand for the fixers, Evidence Removal, and potentially Clemency.

Start small with the Lower Levels Chemist upgrade and the Criminal Network upgrade to give you access to the Black Market, where you'll be able to buy and sell contraband of all levels. From there, I'd invest in the Retired Gunsmith perk, though the rest of that trade's perks make weapons sales legal, so if you're trying to stay on the wrong side of the law, you won't need them. After you buy the store, you can get the Hypertech Smuggler upgrade as well, which can bring you tons of money through high-tier contraband trading.

You'll definitely want a Smuggler's Bay as early as you possibly can from Dr. Jackson, or a few of them; this will let you hide contraband so that inspectors can't find it in your inventory. You can modify them through the Underground Exchange to increase their capacity from a five by five grid to an eight by eight grid for more space.

#4147. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4146. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4145. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4144. Mini Review: Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (Switch 2) - Pleasant But Perplexingly Piecemeal

The latest addition to the pantheon of obscenely long-titled Nintendo Switch 2 Editions is a strange one. Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy takes the Switch 1 game that I have long considered ripe for a new hardware touch-up and does...not a lot with it. It's a chance to revisit one of Nintendo's finest games from the last generation, and the upgrade's price of admission (£7.99 / $9.99) is admittedly a small one, but on the 'new' front, I'm left wanting more.

Let's start with the usual 'Switch 2 Edition' bells and whistles. Pikmin 4 now plays in stunning native 4K resolution docked, and there's added GameShare support for those who want to play some cross-console Dandori Battles with a pal.

If you ask me, Pikmin 4 was already one of the best-looking titles on Switch 1, and the resolution bump doesn't feel transformative. That said, there's no denying that it's even more of a looker on the newer hardware.

Review Pikmin 4 (Switch) - Relaxed, Refined Real-Time Strategy, Ready To Crack The Mainstream

Strangely, the typical Switch 2 givens of a 60fps boost and Mouse Mode are not included this time around. While the former is disappointing, the latter downright confuses me. Nintendo has crowbarred this control scheme in everywhere, but it's absent from a game with a stick-controlled pointer? Even in the co-op Pebble Pitcher mode? Madness!

There's also a new Howl-Out feature that lets you shout commands to Oatchi via the Switch 2 microphone. It's a sweet, if occasionally inconsistent, little bonus that I quickly turned off after realising my real-world dog was getting miffed at me shouting "Good Pup!" without giving him a stroke on the head.

The big newbie is the titular Dandori Academy, where you're tasked with clearing a stage's treasure as quickly as possible. You practice during the week, then take a weekend 'exam', unlocking various medals and in-game rewards in the process. The Dandori stages were a highlight of the base game, and it's great to have even more of them to play here. The three difficulty options provide a welcome challenge in the later stages, and with 72 of them arriving over the next year, it's a wonderful excuse to return to one of my favourite Switch 1 games.

The mode's rollout, however, is a little confusing. 72 new stages sound great on paper, but that means only six new challenges are available each month. If you happen to ace most of them on the first exam weekend, you're left with three weeks of nothing new. Sure, it gives me a prime reason to come back to Pikmin 4 on the regular in 2027, but it does leave things feeling rather slight at launch.

Overall, £8/$10 is a small price to pay for some minor new features and a fun little mode that'll keep me entertained over the coming year, but it's more of a budding shoot right now than the full-bloom upgrade I had dreamed of.

#4143. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4142. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4141. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4139. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4138. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4137. Review: Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2) - An Extraordinary JRPG That Could Use Another Optimisation Pass

A game with the name 'Metaphor' that tackles issues such as culture diversity, democracy, and classism isn't exactly subtle in its delivery, but is just as poignant in 2026 as it was when the game first released in 2024.

Atlus has brought its critically acclaimed turn-based role-playing to Switch 2, and in doing so, reminded everyone of two things: That Atlus are absolute masters at delivering striking stories, endearing characters, and engaging combat through the lens of an incredibly unique art style, and that optimisation for handheld consoles is not their strong suit.

Metaphor: ReFantazio is simultaneously the story of a young boy yearning to reconnect with his dear friend, the prince of the kingdom of Euchronia who had been struck with a curse that left him in a comatose state, a story of prejudice and social manipulation through the kingdom itself, started by the assassination of the king at the hands of Louis Guiabarn, a common-born army officer wanting to challenge the status quo through true meritocracy, AND the story of the parallels between fantasy and reality, using real-life situations as elements of idealistic fantasy within Metaphor's world, things that could never happen for the residents of Euchronia.

The way that Metaphor deftly handles so many threads of varying sizes and scopes is nothing short of extraordinary, especially when the themes of anxiety, willpower, and hope are so striking in the real world.

The individual characters in Metaphor are largely brilliantly written, with their own struggles and demons to battle, even if they aren't party members or sometimes even less important to the overarching plot. Characters like the bat-like Eugief, Heismay, battles prejudice for his race whilst trying to mourn the loss of a family member, but displays his own prejudice against the rabbit-like Papirus for their part in his grief. The stoic Brigitta, owner of the capital's magic igniter shop, casts an icy exterior, only to show her true colours through a puppy she can't resist but take in.

Even the game's main antagonist, Louis, is incredibly compelling, bringing an immediate presence to the screen through his striking design and charismatic dialogue, but as is par for the course, there is far more than meets the eye with Louis. There are a lot of plates to spin in Metaphor, but almost all of them are tantalising events to keep returning to.

It's difficult not to make comparisons between Studio Zero's Metaphor and the Persona series, as they share a lot of DNA: a calendar-based system that has you not only exploring dungeons for treasure and boss fights, but also balancing improvement of social stats, or virtues as they're known here, and bonds with party members and other important NPCs to learn more of their personal stories and gain benefits to the more traditional JRPG aspects of the game in the process.

But Metaphor stands alone in Atlus' repertoire by not only drawing from Persona, but the core Shin Megami Tensei franchise as well, while infusing its own flair in its combat mechanics through the Archetype system.

Archetypes in Metaphor are much closer to the Final Fantasy series' job system than they are to Persona, with each character gaining skills and masteries through use of interchangeable classes gained through the social parts of the game, and combat-earned AP gained to level them up. MAG, a currency gained through both combat and socialisation, can be used to transfer skills from one archetype to another, giving you plenty of ways to experiment with your own builds between the seven party members and the 30 different Archetypes alone.

Combat itself utilises the Turn Icon system resembling core Shin Megami Tensei games, with extra actions gained by striking a critical hit or weakness, or serious losses by missing an attack or hitting an absorbed element. You can also strike at an advantage by attacking enemies in the overworld in real-time, or take them out entirely if you're high enough above them in level (a feature I wish all future JRPGs would carry!), but if an enemy gets the jump on you, it can be devastating. All of these elements combine to make arguably the best combat Atlus has ever put out in a JRPG.

It's also impossible to discuss the game without mentioning its frankly stellar soundtrack. Composer Shoji Meguro's unique flavour is felt throughout the game, with one of the best battle themes to ever grace a JRPG, drawing from Buddhist sutra inspirations with priest Keisuke Honryo's unforgettable chanting.

All of this is to say that Metaphor: ReFantazio is an incredible JRPG, and one that will keep you coming back over and over for well over 80 hours. However, on Switch 2, the experience hasn't come across without a few hiccups along the way.

After releasing Persona 3 Reload on Switch 2 last year, which itself suffered greatly from frame rate issues and muddy visuals, and experiencing inconsistencies with Metaphor: ReFantazio itself in its original release, I was sceptical, to say the least, and that scepticism ended up having merit, as I'm not sure I've seen a game look quite so beautiful and hideous at the same time!

From an artistic standpoint, Metaphor is sumptuous, taking the 'more is more' approach from Persona and applying a much wider colour palette; the UI and menus are stunning, of that there's no doubt. But technically speaking, Metaphor is a bit of a mess.

There are options to run in performance, balanced, or graphics modes both handheld and docked, but regardless of which mode you pick, there were inconsistencies throughout. One moment in combat could look stunning AND run well, and the next cutscene you'd encounter the strangest case of anti-aliasing and fuzzy textures, despite there only being two characters in the room.

Frame rate issues also persist regardless of performance or graphics settings, never enough to overtake the other amazing qualities of the game, but always enough to notice and occasionally distract. Persona 3 Reload did eventually get a performance update that fixed a lot of issues; suffice it to say, I truly hope Metaphor gets one as well!

Additionally, while so much of Metaphor's main dungeons and set pieces are a sight to behold, Atlus's dungeon designs have often left something to be desired, and that's apparent in Metaphor's side dungeons. When on a side quest, it's fairly easy to get turned around in the sea of brown tunnels and foggy forest areas, simply on the back of them all looking identical! It's a stark difference to the Regalith Cathedral, Sandworm's Belly, or Skyrunner main dungeons, for sure.

Metaphor: ReFantazio is an extraordinary JRPG, juggling stories and systems alike with grace and effortlessness, but it is let down somewhat by poor optimisation on Switch 2.

Anyone looking for a huge, sprawling adventure with lovable characters, compelling parallels to the real world, and progression systems that will keep you coming back for more will be far from disappointed with this game, but there's no metaphor for a dodgy frame rate and visuals that can occasionally take you out of the fantasy.

#4136. Feature: Five Reasons Why 2026 Is The Best Time Ever To Be An Xbox Series X|S Owner

The two consoles are celebrating their sixth anniversary on November 10th

We've got a lot of anniversaries taking place over the next few weeks, including the big 25th anniversary of Xbox on November 15th, but we thought we'd first take a moment to celebrate the Xbox Series X|S anniversary as well.

Both of these consoles launched six years ago on November 10th of 2020, and Pure Xbox was there at the time with a big celebration of the launch along with an unboxing preview, a full review, and various bits of coverage.

Hardware Review Xbox Series X - The Fastest, Most Powerful Xbox Ever

A lot has changed over this past six years for Xbox (and indeed, the gaming industry at large), and not all of it has been for the better by any means. As someone who picked up an Xbox Series X at launch though, I reckon 2026 has been the best time ever to own the console, so this seems like a good chance to highlight some reasons why!

Here are those five reasons — in my personal opinion — on why it's so good to own an Xbox Series console right now:

Prior to this year, there had been a lot of disgruntlement amongst the fanbase over the "This is an Xbox" marketing campaign that essentially told us the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S weren't all that important anymore. That might not have been the intention, but it's certainly the impression that many fans came away with.

We've seen a complete change in 2026 though, with Asha Sharma's new leadership team insisting that console is a major focus for them, and implementing an absolute ton of new console-specific features throughout the year. From Mythic Achievements to new startup animations, it's been an amazing year for console updates without a doubt.

The obvious benefit to being an Xbox Series X|S owner this late in the lifecycle is that you get access to a tonne of great games from over the years. 2026 has been an incredible year for new releases too — both first-party and third-party — and I think Xbox Game Pass also enjoyed another really fruitful year complete with many "day one" releases.

My personal backlog is extensive at this point, and it doesn't help that ID@Xbox keeps knocking it out of the park with so many great indie releases on a monthly basis. Xbox Play Anywhere is growing on an extremely impressive scale as well, meaning I can play loads of my purchased Series X|S games on PC whenever I want to.

Despite what some might think, we've had exclusives on Xbox consoles over the past six years, but most of them have been of the third-party variety. Gears of War: E-Day changed all that in October when it become the first permanent console exclusive that Xbox has published in a long time, and it'll be followed up by Clockwork Revolution in 2027.

In other words, you're going to need an Xbox Series X, an Xbox Series S or a powerful enough PC to play these games going forward, which certainly makes these consoles more attractive for fans of certain titles and franchises. I'm certainly comforted knowing that I already own a Series X for when Xbox decides to make even more games exclusive.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to have the biggest video game launch of all time, and that's only going to happen across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There's no PC version whatsoever right now, and fans could be waiting until well into next year until they get a native Windows release of the game.

That automatically makes it a fantastic time to be an Xbox Series X|S owner if you're interested in GTA 6! All of the pre-release footage has been on base PS5, which means it should look basically the same on the Xbox Series X. Everyone's a little bit more concerned about the Series S version, but this is Rockstar we're talking about - they're surely going to pull out all the stops to optimise the biggest game ever for Microsoft's lower-powered console.

It's not usually the case that we're talking about a strong future for six-year-old consoles, but the video game industry isn't in a normal place right now. Everyone knows about the component crisis that's causing prices to vastly increase across the board - something that's affected new purchases of the Series X and S as well.

However, with rumours that Xbox's Project Helix console (potentially set for 2028) could cost well over $1,000, it seems more likely than ever that the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S have still got long futures ahead of them. Combine that with all the new console features that have been added this year, plus the arrival of new technology such as AMD FSR Upscaling 4.1, and it looks like there's a lot more life left in these consoles going forward.

Again, I appreciate that it's not a great time to buy an Xbox Series X or Series S right now due to the aforementioned component crisis, and here's hoping we might at least get some Black Friday deals in a few weeks' time.

For the rest of us who already own one though, this has got to be the best time ever, right? Amazing games, loads of new features, exclusives, GTA 6... I'm very glad to own an Xbox Series X sitting here in November of 2026.

My only fear? That it'll suddenly break and I'll have spend an absolute fortune on a new one.

To me, this is truly incredible. It is more open than the closed ecosystems of my Switch 2 and PS5, which offer portability, but not flexibility across devices.

Of course, there will be some who just dislike Xbox and will never be happy with anything other than the closure of Microsoft. They are best ignored.

#4135. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4134. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

#4133. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

"Creating new and unique products is our top priority"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A Nintendo exec has stressed the importance of creating the company's signature experiences with the rise of AI development.

During a recent investors' meeting attended by multiple Nintendo employees, a question was asked about the company's emphasis on game quality, noting that this, in turn, "seems to be lengthening the development period for each title." The question then poses how Nintendo plans to balance creativity with business management.

Yusuke Beppu, senior executive officer and corporate director for Nintendo, responds, "Development is the engine of Nintendo's competitiveness and value. Creating new and unique products is our top priority," adding that "balancing creativity and business is always challenging." Beppu continues, "Unless we satisfy consumers, our efforts will not lead us to good business results."

Beppu goes on to say that "technologies like the internet and AI have dramatically increased the amount of digital content available to the world," noting the sheer amount of free entertainment available. He also says "we are conducting business in an environment that is different from the past," and that given this increased competition, "it is important to offer unique entertainment experiences that are very Nintendo, so that consumers will choose Nintendo."

With the question itself about Nintendo's lengthy development periods, it's worth noting that Nintendo has been releasing games pretty much every month since the Nintendo Switch 2 launched, sometimes multiple, compared to the likes of Sony and Xbox; I'd say that's pretty fast. With or without AI.

#4131. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. #4130. New TMNT: Splintered Fate Update Adds Even More Reasons To Play In Co-Op

Super Evil Megacorp has been steadily pumping out new content for its TMNT Hades-like, Splintered Fate, ever since launch, and today, the team has added a bunch of new reasons to embark on your roguelike runs in co-op.

The new Shell Squad Co-Op Update goes live today, and as its name suggests, it's all about the multiplayer fun. This free patch adds 24 new co-op powers, eight new co-op tools and eight new co-op masteries, so you can bring the heat to Shredder and the Rat King with even more skills when playing with friends.

The update also includes improved flame visuals, options for character swapping when playing co-op online or locally, and improved Lucky Dice communication.

Here are a few examples of the new powers and tools added in the update:

24x new co-op powers (3 per power tree). Examples: - Passing the Torch - The first player you touch while affected by Rapid Fire also gains its effects, for as long as you have Rapid Fire active. - Shared Warmth - When a player consumes a Splinter's Revive, heal all players. - Chain Reaction - Players' Specials have a chance to trigger a Chain Lightning, dealing Utrom damage per link.

8x new co-op tools (1 per power tree). Examples: - Bubble Trouble - Spawn a bubble on you and the farthest player. The bubble deals Water damage and Freezes enemies, and grants bonus Water damage to players. - Tether Beam - Tether to the closest player. Enemies caught in the beam will take Utrom damage every second. - Shadow Pact - Grant yourself and the closest player a Dark Shell. Each enemy defeated extends it.

8x new co-op masteries (1 per character). Examples: - Donatello - When using your Tool, the closest player becomes invulnerable. - Raphael - When any player lands a critical hit, they have a chance to Multi-crit instead. - Michelangelo - When using your Special, you and the closest player gain a Torrent Strike stack. - Leonardo - When activating your Special, the closest player gains Light Shell.

This one is also available today, so there's no waiting around here, either!

Fortnite Crew and the Rocket League Rocket Pass are notable ones that are only available with Xbox Game Pass Ultimate.

#4128. PS5 Now the Only Console without a Digital Game Gifting Option

If even a Nintendo platform has a digital storefront feature and you don't, then you truly are behind the times. The firm notoriously playing catch-up in this space has today confirmed the Nintendo eShop will be receiving the ability to gift digital games.

The PS Store, which will eventually be the only place you can buy new PlayStation games, still doesn't allow it.

Having downloaded a new system update for the Nintendo Switch 2, the groundwork is laid for a Nintendo eShop gifting feature going live next week. You will be able to gift digital games to people within your Nintendo Account family group.

This implementation is a bit more restrictive than what's on Xbox and Steam, where you can gift digital games to anyone on your friends list. The Nintendo Account family group system, meanwhile, is restricted to a maximum of eight members that all share a single online membership to NSO (Nintendo Switch Online).

Despite the Nintendo approach being less expansive than other storefronts, it's better than nothing.

And nothing is all Sony offers in the digital game gifting space.

Feature 8 Ways Sony Must Improve the PS Store for Our All-Digital Future

From January 2028, PlayStation is going entirely digital with game releases, as it's revealed the production of physical copies for new titles will end. As it leans all the way into the digital space, it makes the PS Store the only place you can buy new PS5 (and potentially PS6 by that point) games.

This has put the PS Store under the microscope, as players now judge the only storefront they'll be able to access new PlayStation releases from. The fact that, as of right now, they wouldn't be able to gift games to their family and friends, is an issue. And now, if the Nintendo Switch 2 can support the feature, there are absolutely no excuses Sony can turn to.

It's one improvement we highlighted in a recent feature that PlayStation really should implement. Other enhancements included a better refund policy, the ability to trade and sell digital games, and a loyalty program.

Currently, the only way you could send a PS5, PS4 game to a family member or friend is by buying them PSN vouchers to redeem. By choosing to focus entirely on digital in the future, Sony must implement a gifting feature where the full process is done entirely on the console.

#4127. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4126. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

Rockstar says GTA 6 will push consoles "to their absolute limits"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 will push PS5 and Xbox Series X|S to "their absolute limits," Rockstar Games says, but that doesn't mean we'll see the game run at 60fps on either platform.

In a new blog post shared today as GTA 6 preloads kick off for those who've pre-ordered digitally, Rockstar discusses what we can expect from the upcoming blockbuster's performance on your platform of choice. However, as previously anticipated, the devs have now confirmed a 30fps cap on both consoles.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life – while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants," Rockstar says.

This is unchanged on PS5 Pro, but owners of Sony's souped-up console can still expect other visual improvements, including ray-traced shadows. "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro," Rockstar adds.

Even those running the game on a regular PS5 can expect a great experience, though, it continues, once again reiterating that line that the game will "play best" on Sony's hardware. The PS5 version has "high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D Audio, and improved load times, making Grand Theft Auto 6 play best on PlayStation 5 consoles."

Rockstar's only mention of Xbox in the blog post is regarding Xbox Cloud Gaming, on which GTA 6 will be available for Series X/S and even Xbox One owners. However, this version will use Series S graphics settings, so don't expect the best-looking version here.

The official confirmation of a 30fps GTA 6 is no doubt going to prove disappointing to some, but it's also not unexpected. After all, the footage shown in the big Netflix Extended Look ran at 30fps, and it was indicated by Rockstar lead Rob Nelson that – at the time of the big media previews – this was the frame rate that the game was running at. Tech analysts have previously stated that 60fps could be a challenge for the game even on PC, so this may be our lot – especially as Rockstar makes no mention of a performance mode to boost those frames on console at a later date.

#4123. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4122. Mini Review: Warhammer Survivors (PS5) - Absurdly Addictive Crossover Is a Match Made in Bullet Hell

Warhammer Survivors is exactly what its name suggests: a Warhammer reskin of Vampire Survivors.

Developed by licensed Warhammer studio Auroch Digital, with Vampire Survivors creator poncle partnering on the project, it's a fantastic, heartfelt adaptation right out of the gate.

Indeed, it's immediately obvious that an awful lot of care has been taken in providing poncle's world-beating gameplay formula with a fresh coat of paint. The Warhammer settings, characters, enemies, and weapons are all there — but the game also relishes in dishing out smaller references to Games Workshop's immensely popular fiction.

In particular, I was left pleasantly surprised by how often Warhammer Survivors pays tribute to the property's tabletop identity. Numerous playable characters, for example, are unlocked by finding miniature figure paints scattered across maps.

Meanwhile, power ups can include rolling damage dice — actual dice — across the battlefield, crushing your foes in the process. You can even drop giant blast radius templates on top of your enemies if you're lucky.

What I'm saying is that Auroch Digital and poncle clearly had loads of fun with this one — it's not just a simple copy and paste job that takes advantage of the Warhammer name.

Oh, and it's basically two games in one. On the main menu, you can pick between Warhammer's dark sci-fi 40,000 setting, and its high fantasy Age of Sigmar setting. Each comes with its own character roster, maps, enemy factions, objectives, upgrades, and everything else, making for a seriously robust package.

Gameplay-wise, the title offers a slight twist on the absurdly addictive Survivors structure. Stages have a 25-minute time limit instead of 30, and I'd say there's a larger emphasis on tactical thinking.

That's because specialised opponents are more prevalent, forcing you to weave your way through the hordes in a more methodical manner. At least, until you rack up so many super-powered upgrades that anything in your path just evaporates anyway.

Yep, that same progression curve that makes Vampire Survivors so insanely moreish is alive and well here, although I do think it takes a little longer to hit those truly chaotic highs because of the aforementioned tweaks.

All in all, Warhammer Survivors perfectly melds Games Workshop's property with poncle's timeless formula, resulting in another exceptional roguelike experience.
